699a84bf8e2052342f79b912 description: I don’t waste time on introductions. If you’re working with me, you earn your place by delivering something useful. Power remains one of the few assets in Tarkov that still holds universal value — even among those pretending they’re above it. Not generators. Not lights. The systems behind them — communications, surveillance, private networks that never truly went dark. Someone is maintaining them. Someone is profiting from them. That position belongs to me. Bring me working components recovered from active zones. If it functions, it has value. If it has value, it belongs in my hands, not abandoned in a ruin.

6848f1776be936dd22573866 description: I’ve observed enough men die in this city to understand what actually ends them. Not poor aim. Not poor instincts. An empty magazine at the wrong moment. Prapor arms soldiers. Skier equips opportunists. I prepare operators to survive sustained violence. That requires capacity. I want magazines built for prolonged engagements — not range toys, not stripped leftovers from men who didn’t last. Bring me equipment that keeps a weapon active longer than the opposition expects.
6848f1776be936dd22573866 startedMessageT: Capacity determines survival. Bring me magazines that extend it.
6848f1776be936dd22573866 successMessageT: Good. More rounds before silence. That’s how professionals remain alive.
684edc10a8af5086d3e6557b description: Distance creates the illusion of competence. It gives weak men time to think, to hide, to convince themselves they’re in control. Factory removes that illusion. No space. No comfort. No clean retreat. Only noise, steel, and decisions made faster than fear can settle. That’s where I measure capability. Not by what is promised, but by what is executed under pressure. Go there. Operate in confined space where hesitation is punished immediately. Show me you can still think when everything around you is collapsing.
684edc10a8af5086d3e6557b startedMessageT: Factory removes excuses. Show me what remains without them.
684edc10a8af5086d3e6557b successMessageT: You maintained control under pressure. That separates you from most.

I identify patterns. Right now, too many conversations are happening without my involvement. That creates imbalance. I correct imbalance. You’ll extend my reach. Place the beacons, expand coverage, and leave without creating a trace. Once I can hear the city clearly, I decide which parts of it remain relevant.

Before this city fractured, I didn’t deal in contracts. I dealt in understanding. Favors exchanged. Protection extended. Access granted — all with the expectation of return.

Some decided those obligations disappeared when Tarkov collapsed. They didn’t. Debt doesn’t vanish. It waits.

One of my secured assets is still sitting in Customs. Green carbon case. Quiet, but valuable. I staged it inside the fortress — under the beds on the first floor.

Now it’s overrun with scavengers.

I don’t send anyone into active noise without preparation. Clear the area first. Ten scavs. Once it’s quiet, you move in, recover the case, and bring it back intact.

You don’t open it. You don’t ask questions.

You will place what’s required and leave without creating a story. If no one notices the route, the route survives. That’s the outcome I’m paying for.

69d81d08b08a9cf2a881f70f description:
Systems don’t drift. Not mine.

Every route, every transfer, every quiet exchange — it’s structured. Monitored. Accounted for. When something changes, it leaves a pattern.

I’ve been watching those patterns.

Missing intervals. Clean extractions where there should have been resistance. Information moving without disruption. That doesn’t come from outside pressure. That comes from inside access.

You’ve been active in the right places. Handling the right materials. Delivering information to the right people.

Skier trades in opportunity. Prapor trades in destruction. Neither of them builds systems like this.

Which means they didn’t find it.

They were fed it.

You’re going to make another adjustment. Small. Precise. Just enough to shift things again.

I want to see what moves when you do.

There it is.

You’ve been moving through my system — handing pieces of it to people who don’t understand what they’re touching.

Skier will sell it. Prapor will burn it.

Both of them think they’re gaining ground.

They’re not.

They’re reacting.

Now I decide what to do with you.
